findings.chapter: Preface (Evidence Discipline panel) vs Ch. 1 §1.1.2/§1.5, Ch. 2 §2.5, Ch. 5 Table 5-2 note, Ch. 6 §6.8; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 Note 1
findings.evidence: PDF p.19 (Preface panel): "ILLUSTRATIVE (Axis 1, provenance) — a non-canonical worked example ([ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED)". PDF p.107 (Ch. 4 Note 1): "[ILLUSTRATIVE] ... is reserved for a non-canonical hypothetical and uses the same ASSUMPTION/DERIVED split." Actual usages of the forbidden pairing: PDF p.27 "not a vendor statement [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]"; PDF p.37 "[ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]" (tokenizer multiplier); PDF p.60 "[ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or bench­mark][HYPOTHESIS][UNMEASURED]"; PDF p.133 "the embedding verdict carries [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]"; PDF p.158 "[ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]" (p95 restoration expectation).
findings.issue: Label-grammar inconsistency: both definitional sites (Preface panel and Ch. 4 Table 4-2 Note 1) state that [ILLUSTRATIVE] pairs only with [ASSUMPTION] or [DERIVED], yet [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] is used at least five times. Ch. 5's Table 5-2 note justifies the pairing by citing "Ch 4, Table 4‑2 note 1", but Note 1's actual text does not license a HYPOTHESIS partner, so the reconciliation mis-cites its own authority and the Preface/Note 1 wording was never amended.
findings.fix_instruction: Amend the Preface panel's ILLUSTRATIVE definition and Ch. 4 Note 1 to "paired with ASSUMPTION, DERIVED, or HYPOTHESIS (the last for non-canonical claims that are reasoned but unvalidated)" — or, alternatively, retag the five [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] instances. Then re-check Ch. 5's Table 5-2 note so its justification cites the amended wording, and sweep the remainder of the book (Chs. 8–26, Appendix A) for further [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS] instances to confirm they match whichever rule is chosen.
